chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ali al-Jarma'i from Durasht al-Wasiti from Ibn Muskhan from Al-Hasan ibn Harun from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'I ate khabeez (fried flour) containing saffron until I was full.' He said, 'When you have completed your rituals and intend to leave Mecca, buy dates with one dirham, then give them in charity; it will be an expiation for what you ate and for what entered upon you during your ihram of which you are unaware.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: Ihram: The sacred state of consecration entered by pilgrims, involving specific clothing and prohibitions.
key_terms.خَبِيص: Khabeez: A traditional dish of flour fried in ghee or oil, often considered a delicacy.
key_terms.زَعْفَرَان: Saffron: A fragrant spice, the consumption of which is prohibited for a muhrim due to its scent.
key_terms.كَفَّارَة: Kaffarah: Expiation or compensation for a religious violation or omission.
key_terms.مَنَاسِك: Manasik: The rituals and rites of Hajj or Umrah.

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim who eats food containing saffron while in ihram?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines the specific expiation (kaffarah) for a pilgrim who consumed saffron, a fragrant substance, while in the state of ihram. The ruling prescribes purchasing dates with one dirham and giving them in charity, serving as atonement not only for the known consumption but also for any unknown violations that may have occurred during the consecration. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the principle of 'unknown violations' (ma la ta'lamu) within the broader framework of Hajj expiations.
